title: Don’t Just Celebrate — Live It — Luke 6:46
paragraphs: Don’t Just Celebrate — Live It — Luke 6:46
Heaven is not impressed by applause that never turns into obedience.
“Why do you call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and not do what I say?” — Luke 6:46

Some people celebrate Jesus with their lips.
Songs.
Posts.
Sunday tears.
But Monday still belongs to the flesh.

That is the tension in Luke 6:46. Jesus is not rebuking atheists. He is confronting people who know the language of faith but refuse the life of surrender. They say the right Name. They feel the right emotions. They wear the right image. But obedience never follows.
Because calling Him Lord is not the same as bowing to Him as Lord.

But here’s what we miss: Jesus is not asking for performance to earn His love. He is calling for obedience that flows from a heart changed by grace. Real faith does not just admire Christ. Real faith follows Him. When Jesus saves a person, He does not only forgive their sin — He begins to rule their life.

That means we do not just celebrate resurrection on a holiday.
We live resurrected on ordinary days.

We forgive when revenge feels sweeter.
We stay pure when temptation feels louder.
We tell the truth when lies feel safer.
We obey when it costs us something.
That is where faith gets real.

And if this verse convicts you, do not run from Jesus.
Run to Him.

Because the same Lord who exposes empty confession is the Savior who welcomes repentant sinners. His blood covers hypocrites who finally stop pretending. His grace rebuilds the heart that has been saying one thing and living another. In Christ, your failure does not have to be the end of your story.

So don’t just celebrate Him.
Live Him.
Follow Him.
Obey Him.
Because in Christ, you already can be.

Prayer:
Lord Jesus, forgive me for the places where my mouth has honored You but my life has resisted You. Teach me to obey from a heart transformed by grace. Make my faith more than words. Make it real. In Your Name, amen.
